title: Puzzling superconductivity in strontium ruthenate: then and now
authors: James F. Annett, Karol I. Wysokiński
abstract: Strontium ruthenate is a very interesting low temperature superconductor with relatively simple normal state and very puzzling superconducting state properties. Despite over thirty years of intensive research, even the precise symmetry of the order parameter is not known. In this paper we briefly review some of the key developments, focussing on some of the newer experiments, especially those which challenged the previous understanding that it is a spin triplet odd parity chiral p-wave superconductor. Since Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ now appears most probably a spin singlet superconductor we have calculated the Kerr effect for one candidate $d$-wave pairing state. We find that for the chiral $d$-wave $E_g$ pairing state the calculated Hall conductance is non-zero and qualitatively similar to that found earlier under the assumption of a chiral p-wave $E_u$ order parameter. We characterize the Hall conductance in relation to two sum rules, one related to Berry curvatures in the Bogoliubov quasiparticle states, and the other $f$-sum rule indicating the presence of inter-orbital pairing.
summary: This paper reviews the decades-long mystery surrounding the superconducting order parameter in $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{RuO}_4$. By analyzing recent experimental data that challenge early spin-triplet models, the authors calculate signatures (like the Kerr effect) for a candidate chiral d-wave singlet state. The work aims to pinpoint the true pairing symmetry by connecting theoretical predictions of transport properties to measurable physical effects.
main_problem: The central problem is determining the precise symmetry of the superconducting order parameter in strontium ruthenate ($	ext{Sr}_2	ext{RuO}_4$), which remains unknown despite decades of research.
main_result: Calculations for a chiral d-wave $	ext{E}_g$ pairing state yield a non-zero Hall conductance, suggesting that the symmetry might be singlet rather than the previously hypothesized triplet state.
method: The authors use theoretical calculations to predict measurable quantities like the Kerr effect and Hall conductance ($\sigma_{xy}(\omega)$) for various superconducting pairing symmetries.
model_or_system: The system is $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{RuO}_4$, a low-temperature superconductor with a well-behaved Fermi liquid normal state. The analysis involves modeling the superconductivity using multi-orbital Hamiltonians and considering different pairing symmetries (p-wave vs. d-wave, spin singlet vs. triplet).
key_observables: Hall conductance ($\sigma_{xy}$), Kerr effect signal, Knight shift, and spin susceptibility $\chi_s(T)$.
important_parameters: Superconducting gap symmetry ($E_g$ state considered), temperature dependence below $T_c$, and the presence/absence of inter-orbital pairing.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing theoretical predictions (e.g., sum rules for $\sigma_{xy}$) against experimental measurements, while acknowledging that simple models may not capture all complexities like spin-orbit coupling effects.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes; the discussion revolves around calculating and interpreting spectral functions related to the Hall conductance and Kerr effect.
paper_structure: The paper reviews historical evidence supporting a chiral p-wave triplet state, presents recent experimental results (Knight shift/$\mu	ext{SR}$) challenging this view towards spin singlet pairing, and concludes by performing new theoretical calculations for a chiral d-wave $	ext{E}_g$ state to predict measurable signatures.
why_interesting: The investigation into unconventional superconductivity symmetry in correlated oxides like $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{RuO}_4$ is highly relevant as it touches upon exotic pairing mechanisms and the interplay between electronic correlations and superconducting ground states, which are key areas of study for many-body physics.
